analysis:
This PR changes only CI threat-review tooling. It does not touch the provider, coordinator contract, attestation, encryption or cache code, so no canonical provider threats (TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041, T-053 etc.) are directly affected.

budget_scan.py (head 85,112,303-305,317-327,332,367,400) adds a `finished` flag. It also adds plan_calls(), which calls an optional paid.plan_calls(count) before each source, depth and integration round. Validation, caching, repair limits and checkpoint ordering are unchanged. plan_calls overwrites active_request and sets paid.last_request={} even when that attribute may be absent; this only affects diagnostics state, not security.

diagnostics.py (head 82-83) exports finished plus the bedrock_call_policy, limit, ceiling and planned_calls keys from the snapshot. These presumably come from paid.metrics() and should be numeric or fixed strings. The adapter source is not supplied, so integration should confirm these values are content-free.

The workflow:
- Removes the workflow_dispatch pr_number path and its API-resolution step. Dispatch now only runs preflight (default true), and the review job runs only on pull_request_target. This reduces the attack surface.
- Keeps fork gating for Bedrock (BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS).
- Raises the job timeout from 20 to 60 minutes and adds THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000.
- Replaces BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_CALLS=12 with BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY=workload and MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS default 500.
- Raises the output-token cap from 4096 to 16384.

The call-budget change is a material billing and availability change. A large same-repo PR, or a fork PR when forks are allowed, could drive up to roughly 500 paid Bedrock calls per run under pull_request_target. Enforcement lives in the unseen Bedrock adapter's plan_calls, which must reject plans beyond the ceiling before any call is made. That code is not supplied, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. This CI cost surface is not modeled in the provider threat model.
